description:
Tier 1 enabler for hashing and crypto kernels (xxh3 and Murmur3-128 use the high half of a 64x64 product; BLAKE3 and bit-set kernels want popcount; decoders want clz/ctz for bit readers). Each is one line of C (__builtin_mul_overflow / unsigned __int128, __builtin_clzll, __builtin_ctzll, __builtin_popcountll) and has an exact Elixir meaning:
- `mulhi(a, b)`: the high 64 bits of the unsigned 128-bit product of a and b taken as u64 bit patterns; Elixir mode: `band(bsr(ua * ub, 64), mask64)` with the sign fix-up to the i64 pattern.
- `clz(x)`, `ctz(x)`: leading/trailing zero count of the u64 pattern, 64 for 0 (C's builtins are undefined at 0, so guard it).
- `popcount(x)`: via :erlang.band loops or a 64-step Elixir function in Elixir mode.

Also decide here whether `rotl64/rotr64` become builtins or stay the bsl/bsr/bor idiom under a mask (clang recognises the idiom; a builtin is clearer in Elixir mode).

Needs defk-w38 (mask idiom) and lands best alongside defk-n4r.2.

Done when: the builtins exist in both modes with agreement properties at 0, 1, -1, i64 min/max and random values, and are listed in docs/language.md.
title: Builtins mulhi, clz, ctz and popcount with exact Elixir meanings
